theory.title: Personality and qualities
theory.explanation: Usa adjetivos para describir el carácter. Para hablar de hábitos, coloca usually, often, sometimes y never antes del verbo principal, pero después de be. Explica opiniones con because. Para habilidades usa be good at / be bad at + sustantivo o verbo en -ing. Compara con more/less + adjetivo + than.
theory.tip: Recuerda: She is always kind, pero She always helps. Después de at, usa un sustantivo o una forma -ing: good at drawing.

content.passage: Our new classmate is called Daniel. He is friendly and quite talkative, but he is never rude. He usually arrives early and often helps other students. Daniel is good at science and he is very creative. His friend Sara is quieter than Daniel. She is patient and careful, and she sometimes helps people with difficult exercises. They get on well because they respect each other. Daniel is more outgoing, but Sara is less nervous when she speaks in front of the class. They are different, but they make a great team.

content.audioTranscript: At school, Mia talks about her two friends. Mia: I get on really well with Alex because he's kind and funny. He usually helps people with their homework. He's good at science, but he's bad at remembering dates. My other friend, Eva, is quieter than Alex. She's always polite and very patient. She sometimes feels shy, but she's never rude. Eva is more creative than Alex, and they both work hard. They are different, but I like them because they are both honest.
